gap: The pane has no tonal step from the page: sidebar and editor are both #f7f7f7, so only a #dfdfdf hairline divides them. A lifts its sidebar to #fdfdfd against a #f9f9f9 page with a lighter #e7e7e7 hairline. B's library reads as part of the page, not a pane beside it.
gapTheirs: The secondary text in the pane is too faint. Dates, previews, the sort control, the count and the status line bottom out at about #999999 (grey 153) on a #fdfdfd sidebar, roughly 2.8:1 contrast. B's are about #8c8c8c (grey 140) on #f7f7f7, roughly 3.2:1. The dates and the two preview lines in A turn washed-out first.
verdict: Both lists have the same bones: search, sort and count, rows with mark, name, date and two lines of preview, and a saved-state line at the foot. The difference is in how the greys are tuned. A's metadata is pale enough that you squint at a date to find last Tuesday's draft. B sets that metadata a step darker, but lets the pane melt into the page so the column has no edge except one hairline. I'd trust B's list for finding a manuscript quickly, but only just.

states.name: search
states.gap: The pane heading 'library' has no chevron. A puts a ▾ after 'Library', which tells you it opens a Location switcher. B's heading is just a folder name, so nothing shows you can change where your manuscripts live.
states.gapTheirs: The pane isn't on the editor's paper. The sidebar is #FDFDFD but the page beside it is #F9F9F9, so there are two whites split by a pale #E7E7E7 hairline. In B the sidebar and editor are both #F7F7F7, divided by a firmer #DFDFDF line, so the library reads as part of the same sheet.
states.verdict: Both libraries are built almost to the same grid: search field, 'Sort by Date', '2 of 8 documents', a cyan bar on the selected row, two grey lines of text per row and a saved-status line at the foot. A lets the pane drift onto its own brighter white, so the file list looks like a panel attached to the editor rather than part of the desk. Its rows are also looser (156 px row pitch against 151) and its preview grey is weaker (#999 against #8C8C8C), so you skim the list less easily. B's heading gives no sign that it's a switcher, which is a real hole, but for looking over a set of chapters B's pane is the steadier one.
secondary: Selected-row band: A #F8F8F8 on #FDFDFD, 148 px tall; B #F2F2F2 on #F7F7F7, 138 px tall. Both are only a 5-level step, which is barely visible
Selection bar: A rgb(0,181,255), B rgb(0,191,255). Both are about 10 px wide and in the same place
Row separator hairline: A #E7E7E7, B #DFDFDF. A's lines almost vanish on its whiter pane
Heading weight: A sets 'Library' in bold, B sets 'library' lighter and smaller, so B's pane heading has less authority over the list
Sort/count baseline: A about 108 px, B about 109 px (display scale). The icon-to-text gap is also 1 to 3 px different in the search row
Status foot: 'In this browser' against 'On this device', same grey and position; B's wording is the one a writer would trust with local files
Not counted as gaps: extensions, faces, heading marker placement and page top, which are all decisions already taken
